title_en: Li Mingbai v. Nanjing Jinling Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over pre-sale contract for commercial housing
ruling_gist_en: 1. full_text_en:
Li Mingbo v. Nanjing Jinling Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over commercial housing pre-sale contract

Ruling Summary

1. For evidentiary materials issued by government organs and other functional departments, the people's court shall examine their authenticity, legality, and relevance to the facts to be proved. If such evidence cannot reflect the objective truth of the case, it shall not be used as the basis for the people's court to determine the facts of the case.

2. Where a seller delivers a house with quality defects, causing the buyer to be unable to use or derive income from the house normally, and the parties have no explicit agreement on how to calculate the actual losses incurred thereby, the people's court may use the contemporaneous rental value of the house as the standard to calculate the buyer's actual losses.

Plaintiff: Li Mingbo, male, 43 years old, Han ethnicity, residing in Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Nanjing Jinling Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at General Road, Jiangning Economic and Technological Development Zone, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Zhao Yuyuan, Chairman of the Board.

The plaintiff Li Mingbo filed a lawsuit with the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, against the defendant Nanjing Jinling Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinling Real Estate Company) concerning a dispute over a commercial housing pre-sale contract.

Plaintiff Li Mingbo alleged: On June 7, 2007, he entered into a commercial housing sales contract with the defendant Jinling Real Estate Company, agreeing to purchase a house located at Room 01, Building 58, Chili Block, Mei Shi Villa, No. 8 General Avenue, Jiangning District, Nanjing. Because the house had quality defects, he had previously filed a lawsuit seeking damages from Jinling Real Estate Company, but at that time he only claimed rental loss incurred before April 20, 2010. He now files this lawsuit again, requesting that Jinling Real Estate Company compensate him for losses of RMB 357,000 (for the period from April 21, 2010 to September 21, 2011, calculated at RMB 21,000 per month), and also compensate him for all expenses paid to the property management company from July 2008 to September 21, 2011, totaling RMB 29,638.

Defendant Jinling Real Estate Company responded: The plaintiff Li Mingbo's claim for rental losses calculated until September 21, 2011, is without basis. After Jinling Real Estate Company reinforced Li Mingbo's house, Li Mingbo failed to cooperate with the inspection, which delayed the issuance of the inspection report. The inspection results showed that the house was fully usable after the reinforcement. Moreover, even if rental losses continued, they should be calculated based on the rental standard determined in the previous judgment. This case and the property management company's claim for property management fees against Li Mingbo are not part of the same contractual relationship. The fact that the house did not meet safe living conditions does not mean Li Mingbo was exempt from paying property management fees. This claim should be dismissed.

The Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing found the following facts at first instance:

On June 7, 2007, the plaintiff Li Mingbo (Party B) and the defendant Jinling Real Estate Company (Party A) signed a commercial housing sales contract for "Mei Shi Villa," stipulating that Party B would purchase from Party A the house at Room 01, Building 58, Chili Block, Mei Shi Villa, No. 8 General Avenue, Jiangning District, with a construction area of 276 square meters. On June 24 of the same year, Jinling Real Estate Company delivered the house to Li Mingbo (the actual construction area was 280.22 square meters). In 2008, Li Mingbo reported to Jinling Real Estate Company that the house had quality defects. On March 18, 2010, Fenggu Building Company prepared structural reinforcement design drawings and an engineering quotation for the house and commenced construction on March 29, 2010, with a construction period of 8 days. After the construction was completed, disputes remained between the parties. Li Mingbo filed a lawsuit, requesting that Jinling Real Estate Company repair the floor slab of the house to meet the qualified standard for safe use and compensate for losses of RMB 500,000. During the trial of that case, Li Mingbo and Jinling Real Estate Company negotiated and agreed to have an appraisal conducted on whether the reinforced floor slab met the qualified standard for safe use; the appraisal institution was Nanjing Jianyan Construction Engineering Appraisal Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jianyan Appraisal Company); and both parties agreed not to challenge the appraisal conclusion on the ground that it was not commissioned by the court. Thereafter, Jinling Real Estate Company commissioned Jianyan Appraisal Company to conduct the appraisal. On March 28, 2011, Jianyan Appraisal Company issued Appraisal Report No. (2011) Jian Jian Zi 5144, concluding that the load-bearing capacity of the first-floor living room floor slab met the requirements of the relevant specifications. Additionally, regarding the rental standard, the first-instance court consulted the Price Certification Center of the Jiangning District Price Bureau, Nanjing. In 2010, the monthly rental price for a similarly located and similarly finished fully decorated house (with a construction area of 240-250 square meters) in the same area as the house in dispute ranged from RMB 7,000 to RMB 8,000, while the rental price for a rough house (with a construction area of 280.22 square meters) was RMB 2,000. From 2007 to 2010, the rental price increase rate was 8%-10%. After hearing that case, the court held that the house delivered by Jinling Real Estate Company had quality defects, rendering Li Mingbo unable to live in or use the house. Therefore, Jinling Real Estate Company should compensate Li Mingbo for the resulting rental losses, which should be calculated up to the time Li Mingbo learned that the house could be safely occupied. The court then ruled in favor of Li Mingbo's claim for rental losses on the house incurred before April 2010 (calculated from July 2008, deducting the renovation period from December 2008 to March 2009).

Now the plaintiff Li Mingbo has filed another lawsuit, requesting the court to order the defendant Jinling Real Estate Company to pay rental losses from April 21, 2010 to September 21, 2011, and other expenses. During the trial, regarding the cut-off date for calculating rental losses, Jinling Real Estate Company failed to provide evidence showing that it had sent Appraisal Report No. (2011) Jian Jian Zi 5144 to Li Mingbo. Based on the trial of the previous case, the parties had cross-examined the appraisal report on July 22, 2011. Li Mingbo argued that after July 22, 2011, a reasonable preparation period should be allowed, so he could claim rental losses until September 21, 2011. Regarding the rental standard, Li Mingbo submitted evidence such as lease agreements and rental invoices, showing that from October 2011 onward, the monthly rental of his house was RMB 21,000. Jinling Real Estate Company argued that the rental standard should be determined based on the court’s inquiry results. In addition, Li Mingbo also claimed from Jinling Real Estate Company property management service fees of RMB 20,522.46, as well as late payment penalties and litigation costs, totaling RMB 29,638. Jinling Real Estate Company argued that these losses were unrelated to this case and were not economic losses it should bear.

The Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing held at first instance:

The commercial housing sales contract signed between the plaintiff Li Mingbo and the defendant Jinling Real Estate Company is valid and legally binding. Because the house delivered by Jinling Real Estate Company had quality defects, Li Mingbo was unable to live in or use it. Therefore, Li Mingbo has the right to claim from Jinling Real Estate Company the losses caused thereby. Since Li Mingbo learned on July 22, 2011, that the house could be safely occupied, the cut-off date for calculating rental losses should be July 22, 2011. Li Mingbo’s assertion that a reasonable preparation period should be granted is without proper basis and is not supported. That is, Li Mingbo may claim rental losses from April 22, 2010 to July 22, 2011. Regarding the calculation standard for rental losses, the court determined it based on the earlier opinion of the Price Certification Center of the Jiangning District Price Bureau, Nanjing: for May 2010 to December 2010, RMB 72,000 (RMB 9,000 per month × 8 months), and for January 1, 2011 to July 22, 2011, RMB 66,660 (RMB 9,900 per month × 6 months and 22 days), totaling RMB 138,660. Regarding Li Mingbo’s second claim, although Jinling Real Estate Company had delivered the house to Li Mingbo in June 2007, due to the quality defects in the house caused by Jinling Real Estate Company, Li Mingbo was unable to use the house normally. Therefore, the property management service fees incurred from July 2008 to November 2008 and from April 2009 to July 22, 2011, can be regarded as losses caused by Jinling Real Estate Company’s breach of contract. Li Mingbo only provided property management fee invoices starting from January 1, 2009. Therefore, for the period before April 2009, Li Mingbo did not provide evidence, so that part is not supported. For the subsequent period, the fees total RMB 18,181.2, which shall be compensated by Jinling Real Estate Company. As for the late payment penalties and litigation costs claimed by Li Mingbo, those shall not be borne by Jinling Real Estate Company.

Accordingly, the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing, in accordance with Article 107 and Article 113, Paragraph 1 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 64, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered judgment on June 13, 2013:

The defendant Jinling Real Estate Company shall compensate the plaintiff Li Mingbo for losses of RMB 138,660 and property management fees of RMB 18,181.2, totaling RMB 156,841.2.

Both Li Mingbo and Jinling Real Estate Company were dissatisfied and appealed to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court:

(1) The first-instance judgment’s calculation standard for rental losses lacks factual and legal basis. The so-called “opinion of the Price Certification Center of the Jiangning District Price Bureau” was merely a personal opinion of a staff member, without any data supporting that staff member’s view. The appellant has already provided lease contracts and invoices for the same area, which are sufficient to prove that the market rental price of his house at that time should not be lower than RMB 21,000.

(2) Calculating losses until July 22, 2011, does not reflect the actual circumstances of the loss. The appellant received the appraisal report on July 22, 2011, and could not move in on the same day. Renovation and finishing were necessary, and this period is causally related to the quality defects in the house.

(3) There is evidence supporting the property management fees incurred before April 2009.

Jinling Real Estate Company appealed: (1) The first-instance court erred in holding that, because Jinling Real Estate Company failed to provide evidence of mailing the appraisal report to Li Mingbo, the cut-off date for calculating rental losses should be July 22, 2011. After the reinforcement, the house was fully usable. The appellee’s failure to cooperate with the inspection caused unnecessary expansion of losses, which should be borne by him alone. (2) The first-instance judgment’s ruling that Jinling Real Estate Company should compensate Li Mingbo for property management losses was improper.

After the second instance, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found at first instance.

During the second instance, the appellant Li Mingbo submitted a copy of the stub of an invoice for public electricity fees collected by the property management company on behalf of the owner, dated July 10, 2013, in the name of Chili 58-1 Li Mingbo, for RMB 561; a detailed list of shared electricity fees for Chili 58-1 from September 2008 to April 2013, prepared on July 11, 2013; and a copy of an invoice for property management fees for 2008 (January to December) in the amount of RMB 4,612, issued by the property management company on November 28, 2008, in the name of Chili 58-1. These were submitted to prove that he had paid the relevant fees and the fee standards. The appellant Jinling Real Estate Company acknowledged the authenticity of this evidence.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held at second instance: The commercial housing pre-sale contract between the appellant Li Mingbo and the appellant Jinling Real Estate Company is valid and legally binding, and both parties shall perform accordingly. Because the quality defects of the house prevented Li Mingbo from using and deriving income from the house, Jinling Real Estate Company shall compensate Li Mingbo for the related losses. Regarding the calculation standard for rental losses, the first-instance court’s determination based on the earlier opinion of the Price Certification Center of the Jiangning District Price Bureau was relatively reasonable. Li Mingbo’s request to calculate rental losses from May 2010 to July 2011 based on the rental price after December 2011 is not supported. Regarding the cut-off date for losses, based on the facts found at first instance, the parties cross-examined the appraisal report on July 22, 2011, and it was only then that Li Mingbo saw the appraisal report of Jianyan Appraisal Company. The first-instance court’s determination of the cut-off date as July 22, 2011, was relatively reasonable. Therefore, Jinling Real Estate Company’s appellate arguments are not supported by the court. Because the appraisal report indicated that the house was habitable, Li Mingbo’s appellate arguments are not adopted by the court. Regarding whether property management fees should be compensated as losses, because the house delivered by Jinling Real Estate Company did not meet the contract quality standards, Jinling Real Estate Company shall compensate Li Mingbo for the property management fee losses. Therefore, Jinling Real Estate Company’s appellate arguments are not adopted by the court. The new evidence submitted by Li Mingbo during the second instance can prove that the property management fees he paid from July to November 2008 amounted to RMB 1,922 (RMB 4,612 ÷ 12 × 5). This amount falls within the time period claimed in his original lawsuit (excluding the renovation period from December 2008 to March 2009), and the court supports this. For property management fee claims exceeding the time period in his original complaint, the court will not address them. For the appeal regarding public electricity fee losses, this was not raised in the original complaint, so that part is not addressed.

In summary, because the appellant Li Mingbo provided new evidence during the second instance, the amount of property management fees to be compensated in the original judgment shall be changed to RMB 20,103.2, which, together with the rental losses of RMB 138,660, totals RMB 158,763.2. In accordance with Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court rendered judgment on November 8, 2013:

1. Revoke the Civil Judgment (2012) Jiang Ning Kai Min Chu Zi No. 808 of the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing; 2. Jinling Real Estate Company shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, pay in a lump sum compensation to Li Mingbo in the amount of RMB 158,763.2.

Li Mingbo remained dissatisfied and applied to the Jiangsu High People's Court for retrial, with the same grounds as his appellate arguments.

During the review of the retrial application, the Jiangsu High People's Court obtained from the Nanjing Municipal Bureau of Housing and Urban-Rural Development the rental prices for multiple villas in the Chili Block of Maslande, No. 8 General Avenue, Jiangning District, for the years 2010 to 2012. The investigation showed that the comprehensive average rental unit price for villas in that block was: RMB 61.36 per square meter per month in 2010, and RMB 67.82 per square meter per month in 2011. Based on these standards, the monthly rental price for the house in dispute was RMB 17,194.3 in 2010 and RMB 19,004.52 in 2011. It was also found that Article 12 of the Commercial Housing Sales Contract signed by the parties stipulated that if quality defects within the warranty period caused economic losses to Party B (Li Mingbo), Party A (Jinling Real Estate Company) shall be responsible for repair and replacement, and shall bear the actual and direct losses caused to Party B. However, the contract did not clearly specify how to calculate the actual direct losses. During the review period, the Jiangsu High People's Court arranged for both parties to cross-examine the above evidence.

The Jiangsu High People's Court held upon review: The people's court shall make judgments based on the facts of the case as proved by evidence. Whether evidence is provided by the parties or obtained by the people's court ex officio, it must objectively and truthfully reflect the facts of the case, and only after being cross-examined by both parties can it be used as the basis for determining the facts. For evidentiary materials such as inquiry opinions and consultation opinions issued by government organs and other functional departments, the people's court shall examine their authenticity, legality, and relevance to the facts to be proved. If such evidence cannot reflect the objective truth of the case, it shall not be used as the basis for the people's court to determine the facts of the case. In this case, Jinling Real Estate Company breached the contract by delivering a house with quality defects, rendering Li Mingbo unable to live in it normally, and thus shall bear liability for breach of contract. Li Mingbo’s request to calculate his actual losses resulting from the quality defects based on the contemporaneous rental value of the house should be supported by the people's court. Regarding the calculation standard for rental losses, the lower courts used the consultation opinion of the Price Certification Center of the Jiangning District Price Bureau as the rental standard for the house in dispute, calculating the rental losses for 2010 at RMB 9,000 per month and for 2011 at RMB 9,900 per month. According to general market conditions, the factors determining the rental price of a house mainly include area, layout, location, decoration grade, and surrounding environment. The inquiry opinion issued by the Price Certification Center of the Price Bureau is merely a reference and evidentiary material for determining the rental price of a house and should not become the direct basis for determining the rental standard for the house in dispute. According to the facts ascertained by the court, the rental standard provided by the Price Certification Center of the Price Bureau was far lower than the actual market rental price for comparable houses in the Mei Shi Villa area. Therefore, the inquiry standard did not reflect the actual circumstances of the rental market price for the house in dispute at the time. Consequently, the lower courts’ exclusive reliance on the inquiry standard from the Price Bureau to determine the actual rental losses for the house in dispute was clearly unfair. When calculating the actual rental losses for the house in dispute, the true circumstances of the market rental price should be comprehensively considered. Although the lease agreements submitted by Li Mingbo for the same area showed that some owners in the community had achieved monthly rental prices of over RMB 21,000, those rental prices were negotiated individually based on the specific location and decoration of each owner’s house, combined with the actual needs of the tenants, and were not representative.

Based on the above facts and reasoning, the Jiangsu High People's Court rendered a ruling on October 8, 2014, holding that Li Mingbo’s retrial application met the circumstances specified in Article 200, Items (1) and (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and ordered the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court to retry this case. The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court rendered a ruling on December 18, 2014: Revoke the Civil Judgment (2013) Ning Min Zhong Zi No. 2605 of the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court and the Civil Judgment (2012) Jiang Ning Kai Min Chu Zi No. 808 of the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing, and remand the case to the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing for retrial.

**Nanjing Jiangning District People's Court, upon retrial at first instance, held that:** the pre-sale contract for commercial housing entered into between the plaintiff at first instance, Li Mingbai, and the defendant at first instance, Jinling Real Estate Company, was lawfully valid, and both parties should perform in accordance with the contract. Due to the quality problems of the house, Li Mingbai was unable to use and derive income from the house in question. Jinling Real Estate Company should compensate Li Mingbai for the resulting losses in rent and property management fees. Comparing the price inquiry opinions from the pricing authority with the rental register of villas in the same area obtained by the higher-level court, the disparity was significant. The rental unit price reflected in the latter better represented the true rental price of the house in question at the time and should be adopted. With respect to the rental loss from April 21 to December 2010, the court discretionarily determined it to be RMB 143,229 (61.36 × RMB 280.22/month × 8.33 months); for the rental loss from January 1 to July 22, 2011, the court discretionarily determined it to be RMB 127,330 (67.82 × RMB 280.22/month × 6.7 months); the total for the above is RMB 270,559. The property management fee loss of RMB 1,922 paid by Li Mingbai for the period from July to November 2008 (after deducting the decoration period from December 2008 to March 2009) and the property management fees of RMB 18,181.2 paid from April 2009 to July 22, 2011, should be compensated by Jinling Real Estate Company.

Pursuant to Article 44, paragraph 1, Article 60, paragraph 1, Article 107, and Article 113 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 64, paragraph 1, and Article 207 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Nanjing Jiangning District People's Court rendered the following retrial first instance judgment on April 23, 2015:

1. The defendant at first instance, Jinling Real Estate Company, shall, within ten days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective, compensate the plaintiff at first instance, Li Mingbai, for losses totaling RMB 290,662.2 (including rental loss of RMB 270,559 and property management fee loss of RMB 20,103.2). After deducting the RMB 160,322.12 already paid by Jinling Real Estate Company to Li Mingbai after the original judgment took effect, the defendant at first instance, Jinling Real Estate Company, shall additionally compensate the plaintiff at first instance, Li Mingbai, for losses of RMB 130,340.08.

2. The remaining claims of the plaintiff at first instance, Li Mingbai, are dismissed.

Both Li Mingbai and Jinling Real Estate Company were dissatisfied with the retrial first instance judgment and appealed to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court.

**The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, upon retrial at second instance, held that:** Because the house delivered by Jinling Real Estate Company had quality problems, rendering it impossible for Li Mingbai to live in it normally, Li Mingbai's claim for compensation for losses is in accordance with the law. Regarding the issue of the standard for calculating losses, although the house lease agreement submitted by Li Mingbai showed that some owners in the relevant residential community could lease their houses at a monthly rent of over RMB 21,000, this rental price was not representative. In contrast, the prices recorded in the rental register of villas in the same area obtained by the Jiangsu High People's Court from the Nanjing Municipal Housing and Urban-Rural Construction Bureau represented the average rental price determined by integrating multiple factors, and were more representative. On the basis that neither party applied for an assessment of the rental price of the house before and after decoration, the retrial first instance court's reference to the rental prices determined in that register, in light of the specific circumstances of the house, was not improper. Li Mingbai's request for compensation at a rate of at least RMB 21,000 per month cannot be supported. In summary, the facts found in the retrial first instance judgment were clear, and the judgment rendered was not improper. The appeal claims of both Li Mingbai and Jinling Real Estate Company cannot be established and are not supported.

Pursuant to Article 170, paragraph 1, subparagraph (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court rendered the following retrial second instance judgment on September 25, 2015:

**Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.**

This judgment is final.
